# Submission Plan & Journal Synthesis: Margie & 9 Comparable U.S. Literary Journals

---

### Critical Status Update on Margie / The American Journal of Poetry
* **Official Submissions Page:** [The American Journal of Poetry Submission Manager (Submittable)](https://xxxtheamericanjournalofpoetry.submittable.com/submit) *(kept open in Tab 1675924496)*.
* **Submission Method:** Submittable.
* **Fee Status:** None currently active ($0), as calls are shut down (historically charged a submission fee).
* **Reading Period / Stated Window:** **Closed / Inactive.** The live Submittable page states: *"There are presently no open calls for submissions."* Furthermore, the journal’s original domain (`theamericanjournalofpoetry.com`) has expired and lapsed into third-party commercial spam, and industry records confirm the journal permanently ceased accepting submissions in January 2022.
* **Simultaneous Submissions & Packet Limits:** *Not shown* on the live Submittable page (historically allowed simultaneous submissions and favored packets up to 6 poems with an emphasis on long poems and "Strong Rx Medicine").

---

## 1. Comprehensive Master Table (10 Journals)

| # | Journal | Submission Method | Fee / No-Fee | Reading Period / Window | Simultaneous Submissions | Packet Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Margie / The American Journal of Poetry** | Submittable | Free ($0 currently; calls closed) | **Closed** ("There are presently no open calls for submissions") | *Not shown* on live page | *Not shown* on live page |
| 2 | **Rattle** | Submittable (or postal for incarcerated / without internet) | **Free / No-fee** ($0 for general poems; $30 for annual prizes) | **Year-round** ("Submissions are open year-round, always welcomed, and always free") | **Allowed & encouraged** | Up to 4 poems (or pages of short poems); any length |
| 3 | **The Adroit Journal** | Submittable (email for writers with disabilities) | **Free / No-fee** ($0 for regular poetry) | **Active open window** through Sun, Nov 1, 2026 (7:00 AM) | **Allowed** (must specify & notify upon acceptance) | Up to 6 poems in 1 document; no length limits |
| 4 | **Palette Poetry** | Submittable | **Free / No-fee** for Featured Poetry ($0; $20 for contests) | **Year-round** ("ALWAYS FREE. ALWAYS OPEN. Open year-round") | **Allowed** (must notify via Submittable upon acceptance) | Up to 5 poems, max 10 pages total, in 1 document |
| 5 | **Frontier Poetry** | Submittable | **Free / No-fee** for New Voices ($0; paid fast-track optional) | **Year-round** ("Always open. Always free.") | **Allowed** (must notify upon acceptance) | Up to 5 poems, max 10 pages total, in 1 document (for emerging poets: ≤1 book) |
| 6 | **Diode Poetry Journal** | Email (`diodepoetryjournal@gmail.com`) | **Free / No-fee** ("we do not charge a reading fee") | **Year-round** ("Submissions are accepted year-round") | **Allowed** (must notify immediately upon acceptance) | 3–5 poems in 1 Word doc, PDF, or email body; no line limit stated |
| 7 | **Waxwing Literary Journal** | Submittable | **Free / No-fee** ($0; 300/mo queue cap) | **Open in April, May, October, November** (Reopens Oct 1) | **Allowed & encouraged** | 1–5 poems in 1 document |
| 8 | **The Cincinnati Review** | Submittable (or postal for disabled / incarcerated) | **Free / No-fee** ($0 for regular poetry; fee only for Schiff contest) | **September, December, May** (opens 1st of month until cap); miCRo open nearly year-round | **Allowed** (must withdraw or message via Submittable) | Up to 5 poems, max 10 pages total (miCRo: up to 3 poems, ≤32 lines each) |
| 9 | **Shenandoah** | Submittable | **Free / No-fee** ($0; 800/mo cap across genres) | **Announced seasonally** ("POETRY reading periods for the 2026-27 academic year will be announced shortly") | **Allowed** (must withdraw immediately if accepted) | 3–5 poems, max 10 pages total |
| 10 | **Ninth Letter** | Submittable (or postal) | **$3 reading fee** for print (fee-free window Dec 1–31; hardship waiver via email) | **Print:** Sept 1 – Feb 28; **Web:** Sept 1 – Nov 1 & Feb 1 – Apr 1 | **Allowed & welcomed** | Print: 3–5 poems, max 8 pages; Web: up to 3 poems |

---

## 2. Three-Tier Packet Strategy & Aesthetic Recommendations

### Bucket 1: Top 4 Best First-Wave Submissions
*These journals combine open reading windows, zero submission fees, high national reach/prestige, and explicit encouragement of simultaneous submissions.*

1. **Rattle** *(Tab 1675924600: Guidelines; Tab 1675924601: Sample)*
   * **Why First Wave:** Open year-round, free to submit, paying ($200 print / $100 web), rapid/reliable circulation, and explicitly encourages simultaneous submissions.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Strongly favors accessible, narrative, emotive, musical, and human-grounded poetry. If your packet has a **literary/traditional voice**, accessible free verse, formal discipline, or witty/candid observational power (as seen in Eric Burger’s *God’s Razors* and Jane Hirshfield's work), *Rattle* is the single best landing spot. It avoids deliberately opaque or insular academic avant-garde in favor of poems that move, illuminate, or speak directly to the human condition.
2. **The Adroit Journal** *(Tab 1675924611: Guidelines; Tab 1675924612: Sample)*
   * **Why First Wave:** Free regular submissions, active reading window open through November 1, paying ($50/poem), and high prestige among contemporary lyric poets.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Balances **experimental and contemporary lyric voices**. Recent issues (e.g., Issue 52 featuring Shane McCrae, Kathy Fagan, Nate Marshall) showcase lush figurative language, syntactical dexterity, identity, cultural poetics, and sharp, inventive lineation. Exceptional target if your work blends formal intelligence with striking modern metaphors.
3. **Palette Poetry** *(Tab 1675924602: Guidelines; Tab 1675924603: Sample)*
   * **Why First Wave:** "Always open, always free" for Featured Poetry, paying ($50–$150), generous 5-poem / 10-page packet limit, rapid turnaround.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Welcomes both **vivid lyric traditionalism and experimental craft**. Recent samples (Yuhan Wu's *Plum Rain Season*, Chloé Leisure's *Produce, Bear, Surrender*, and Eva Mary Hooker's *Aubade*) show an affinity for striking imagery, vulnerability, sensory-rich landscapes, and existential reflections.
4. **Frontier Poetry** *(Tab 1675924604: Guidelines; Tab 1675924605: Sample)*
   * **Why First Wave:** Free year-round submissions for new and emerging poets (≤1 published full-length collection), paying ($50/poem), and fast response window (8–12 weeks).
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Ideal for **contemporary lyric and narrative discovery**. Samples (Anders Villani's *Poison*, Eduardo Martinez-Leyva's *Don’t Look Back, Little Halo*) favor visceral emotional honesty, intimate voice, narrative clarity, and dynamic lineation.

---

### Bucket 2: Next 3 Worth Sending (Second Wave)
*These journals offer top-tier curation and zero fees, but have either specific submission mechanics (email), tight seasonal reading windows, or strict monthly volume caps.*

5. **Diode Poetry Journal** *(Tab 1675924599: Guidelines; Tab 1675924608: Sample)*
   * **Logistics:** Completely fee-free, open year-round, fast response (often 5–30 days), accepts simultaneous submissions, but uses **direct email submission** (`diodepoetryjournal@gmail.com`) rather than Submittable.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Strongly tilted toward an **experimental and visually innovative voice**. As explicitly stated in their guidelines and demonstrated in Volume 19 Nos. 1 & 2, *Diode* actively seeks narrative experimental, visual, found, and erasure poetry, hybrid forms, and boundary-pushing poetics. Perfect if your packet contains daring, non-linear, or formally inventive poems.
6. **Waxwing Literary Journal** *(Tab 1675924609: Guidelines; Tab 1675924610: Sample)*
   * **Logistics:** Free to submit, highly regarded, but operates on a **strict calendar schedule** (Poetry reading periods are April, May, October, November) and caps submissions at 300 total per month. Non-paying.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Superb balance of **lyric tradition and inventive global poetics**. Issue XXXVI (featuring Jenny Molberg, Alonso Llerena, Kelli Russell Agodon, and Rosebud Ben-Oni) demonstrates a dedication to cultural breadth, precise craft, linguistic elegance, and subtle formal experimentation. Submit on October 1 right when the portal opens.
7. **The Cincinnati Review** *(Tab 1675924614: Guidelines; Tab 1675924617: Sample)*
   * **Logistics:** Prestigious university journal paying $30/page for print poetry and $25 for miCRo; free regular submissions. However, print reading periods are tightly restricted to September, December, and May (closing when caps are reached), though the miCRo series (≤32 lines) is open almost year-round.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Favors a **refined literary voice with tight structural compression**. Recent miCRo poems like Michael Eyre’s *Birth Equinox* demonstrate exquisite control of caesura, repetition, and quiet musical meditation. Ideal for polished, formally exacting, and structurally disciplined poems.

---

### Bucket 3: Lower-Priority or Situational Targets
*Journals with fees, unannounced reading windows, or inactive status.*

8. **Ninth Letter** *(Tab 1675924615: Guidelines; Tab 1675924618: Sample)*
   * **Why Lower Priority:** Charges a **$3 submission fee** on Submittable for print submissions (though fee is waived in December and hardship waivers can be requested by email; postal submissions are free).
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Emphasizes **formal experimentation, hybridity, and nontraditional subject matter**, alongside traditional literary work. Their web and print archives (e.g., Emily Skaja, Kara Candito) showcase sharp, image-dense, daring voice. Worth submitting in December when the fee is waived or if you send a postal packet.
9. **Shenandoah** *(Tab 1675924613: Guidelines; Tab 1675924616: Sample)*
   * **Why Situational:** Zero-fee and high prestige, but poetry submissions are **currently on hold** awaiting the 2026–27 reading window announcement ("POETRY reading periods for the 2026-27 academic year will be announced shortly") and capped at 800 submissions/month.
   * **Aesthetic Fit:** Welcomes both **traditional/formal mastery and energetic risk-taking**. Volume 75 No. 2 (guest-edited by Samyak Shertok, featuring Zeina Hashem Beck, Victoria Chang, Jacqueline Osherow, and Erika Meitner) showcases ghazals, golden shovels, sonnets, and bold contemporary voice. Keep watch for their window opening.
10. **Margie / The American Journal of Poetry** *(Tab 1675924496: Guidelines)*
    * **Why Lowest Priority:** **Completely inactive / permanently closed.** Do not submit here; keep the Submittable page only as reference evidence. Use *Rattle*, *The Adroit Journal*, and *Palette Poetry* as the true direct heirs to Margie’s aesthetic of bold, risk-taking, expansive poetic voices.
